name: Paseah
overview: Paseah is a male figure mentioned in the book of Nehemiah, identified primarily as the father of Joiada. There is no tribal affiliation or additional personal notes recorded about him in Scripture. His mention is brief and centers on his paternal relationship.
namesAndTitles: The name Paseah is a proper name that means 'hobbling one.' This meaning is noted in the Hebrew context but does not appear to have been given by God. The name's significance beyond its literal meaning is not elaborated in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Paseah as the father of Joiada, as indicated in Nehemiah 3:6. Beyond this paternal connection, no other family relationships are documented for Paseah.
scriptureSignificance: Paseah's significance in the biblical narrative is tied to his role as the father of Joiada, who is mentioned in the context of the rebuilding efforts in Nehemiah. His mention helps establish genealogical and communal connections during the post-exilic restoration period. Although Paseah himself does not have a detailed narrative, his inclusion contributes to the historical record of those involved in the restoration of Jerusalem.
